reasoning: One act: a question. The person wants to know how long the running job will take so they can decide whether to wait — they are asking for information, not for anything to be done. The Director answers it; a question creates nothing, opens no spec, writes no row. Fetching the fact (elapsed time, expected duration) is reading, not work, and the effort of answering never converts the question into a task. Nothing is in flight that this changes: the job keeps running toward the same goal, so this is neither a correction nor a halt — asking about the state of work does not change what that work must do. A turn that accepted no work names no dimension and calls no specialist. What the person hears back is the answer, and that they were answered.
